read: On 34 solo-wrong cases, the flash-lite holdout adopts the wrong answer 0.2353 under two unanimous wrong peers but only 0.1176 when one of the two instead asserts the CORRECT answer (a single dissenter), a directional reduction of 0.1177. This is CONSISTENT with the classic Asch finding that a single ally breaks conformity (the deference depends on a unanimous board), but it is NOT significant at this sample size (paired McNemar gain=5 lose=1, p=0.21875; only 6 discordant cases): n is capped at the 34 solo-wrong cases in the scanned set. Reported honestly as a suggestive-but-underpowered dissenter effect; a larger solo-wrong pool (or a lower-baseline-accuracy set) would be needed to confirm it.
